title: System safety tradeoffs for Q3 release cadence
topics: cost vs latency tradeoffs for Q3 launch cadence
summary: Cross-functional huddle to align release pace for Q3 features (dedicated quant path, new batching heuristics) vs system safety and SLOs. Decided to conservative rollout with staged quantization windows and concrete rollback criteria; finance and legal asked for clear audit and cost forecasts. Action items assigned for perf benching, audit doc drafts, and a canary schedule.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Samira, Leo, Jordan, Raj, Emily, Mateo, Anika
-- Auto-generated summary: cross-functional release safety tradeoffs

[00:00] Priya K: okay, uh, starting. Thanks everyone for making time, I know this is a packed week. The goal for today is to align on the Q3 release cadence specifically where it intersects with system safety — things like SLOs, rollback criteria, and the quantization windows that Leo's team is proposing.

[00:22] Ethan P: yeah, I'll be brief on the infra constraints. We have the new batcher landing next week, but we still see tail latency variance on the 16K traces. So any aggressive rollout needs a safety net, otherwise we very likely hit p95 violations.

[00:41] Samira N: just to add, our incident playbook assumes fallback to smaller model variant + cache bypass, but we haven't tested that in the wild with the prefix-K V cache behavior — sorry, K V spelled out — prefix K V cache, and the quantized kernels. There may be a mismatch.

[01:05] Leo M: right, the quant-profile-P3 that ML suggested reduces token-cost by about 28% in our sim, but on longer contexts we saw occasional token hallucination spikes; I want to caution we need a quality gate.

[01:28] Jordan L: what does 'hallucination spikes' look like? is it steady drift or occasional outliers?

[01:38] Leo M: mostly outliers but when they happen they are catastrophic for user UX — e.g., wrong named entities repeated — and the scoring model flags them but there's lag.

[01:52] Priya K: okay so two constraints: (1) infra can't accept frequent p95 regressions, and (2) product/qa can't ship without quality gates. We need to decide cadence: aggressive Q3 feature set shipped across all regions July 15th-ish, or staged with dedicated canaries and a slower runway.

[02:15] Raj P: finance perspective: aggressive rollout reduces unit cost earlier, but if we hit a regression we'll have re-run costs and potential revenue impact. Need a delta on cost vs risk.

[02:30] Emily C: legal asks for clarity on audit logs and KMS usage for Private customers. If we're quantizing models or changing kernels, we must document model artifacts and key handling changes for SOC2 audit.

[02:46] Anika B: release manager here — my concern is scheduling. We already have two major launches in that July window; adding a risky quant rollout increases oncall load. We need explicit rollback triggers.

[03:03] Priya K: proposed plan: three-phase approach — alpha internal canaries (small traffic), external canaries (5–10% in non-critical regions), then gradual ramp if metrics stable. Each phase has a list of gating metrics: p95 latency, error rate, quality regressed @ 99% pass on eval set. Thoughts?

[03:28] Ethan P: sounds fine but we need concrete thresholds. p95 <= 230ms (current baseline 210ms), error-rate increase < 0.2%, and KV cache hit ratio maintained within 3% — those are rough.

[03:47] Samira N: agree on thresholds, but add a blast radius clause: if quality regressions appear in more than 3% of sampled sessions, immediate rollback.

[04:03] Leo M: on the eval set — we need to expand it for long-context prompts. Current eval is 1k prompts, mostly 512-token. I'll run a 5k set with 8k and 16k sequences to catch long-tail.

[04:20] Jordan L: can you include rate-limited sequences and KV-cache cold starts in those tests? Those are often where the worst behavior shows.

[04:32] Leo M: yep will include cold vs hot cache buckets.

[04:40] Priya K: okay, operationally, Samira, can SRE run perf bench across the quant profile and current float baseline? Need both cold and warmed KV cache runs.

[04:52] Samira N: yes, I'll schedule 8k/16k runs. I'll capture p50/p95/p99 and tail CPU/GPU mem, and raw logs. Expect results by next Wed. Quick note — in past runs the quant kernels had different memory spill patterns, so watch for OOMs in high concurrency.

[05:18] Raj P: on cost, please provide both unit cost and expected monthly savings. We need to show CFO both best-case and worst-case scenarios to sign off on reserved capacity changes.

[05:30] Emily C: from compliance, if we're changing model artifacts we need a change log per model version and a signoff from research/ML. Also KMS rotation and HSM usage must be captured if keys used for private infra.

[05:46] Mateo R: ops question — if we roll back, what is our time-to-restore? Do we have a fast path that doesn't require database schema changes?

[05:56] Ethan P: rollback for model variant is fairly fast, but if we've done kernel changes or quantized saved artifacts that require a compatible runtime, we have to ensure the fallback runtime is available on the fleet. That is something we must pre-stage.

[06:12] Priya K: pre-stage fallback runtime — action item for infra. Anika, can you add that to the release checklist?

[06:19] Anika B: yes, will add; question on canary windows — should we reserve two-hour windows each day for the first week?

[06:28] Samira N: two-hour windows are fine but we need oncall. I'll coordinate roster. Also recommend a read-only telemetry snapshot for the first hour to avoid alert storm.

[06:40] Priya K: Good. Now let's talk about quality gating specifics — Leo, what's the scoring threshold?

[06:48] Leo M: propose automatic gating: quality regression measured by our paraphrase-and-precision metric — require F1 drop < 1.2% and hallucination count below threshold. But manual review must be triggered if automated metric shows fail for >0.5% of sessions.

[07:06] Jordan L: can we implement an automatic rollback trigger or do we prefer manual stop? Auto rollback is risky, but automatic throttling to 0-1% can reduce blast.

[07:17] Priya K: hybrid — automatic throttle to 2% if metrics degrade, then manual decision to full rollback. This reduces user impact but keeps humans in the loop.

[07:29] Emily C: make sure the throttle action and rollback triggers are documented for audit. We'll need an approval trail.

[07:38] Raj P: finance also wants a soft cap on monthly burn for the first 90 days so we can cap exposure. Maybe reserve a safety budget line.

[07:48] Priya K: noted — Raj to propose numbers.

[07:55] Ethan P: one technical unknown — the new kernel selection logic sometimes picks a fallback kernel under high concurrency that is not quant-friendly. Need to lock kernel selection policy for rollout.

[08:07] Leo M: that's the kernel-pick heuristic; we can pin kernels for the canary fleet. But that increases management overhead.

[08:16] Samira N: pinning is OK for a short window. We'll have a script to enforce kernel pin on the canary nodes. Add to infra action items.

[08:24] Priya K: let's capture concrete gating matrix in the playbook: list metric, threshold, sampling window, action. I'll draft and circulate.

[08:33] Anika B: also include the rollback runbook steps and the comms plan for customers and internal teams.

[08:40] Priya K: Emily, legal to approve comms text?

[08:44] Emily C: yes, will provide a short template for customer notifications and internal postmortem templates.

[08:50] Priya K: okay time check — we've got alignment on cadence and gating. Any final open risks?

[08:58] Leo M: residual risk: quality drift on domain-specific prompts we don't have in eval; recommend a small pilot with selected beta customers.

[09:08] Raj P: risk: cost spike if traffic shifts to more expensive runtime unexpectedly. Also contract exposure for big customers.

[09:16] Priya K: decided: do internal alpha next week, external beta with 5% traffic in a low-risk region two weeks after, then ramp. Action items assigned — see the list.

[09:28] Samira N: will run perf by Wed.

[09:33] Leo M: will run quality reg by Tue.

[09:37] Priya K: Priya to publish playbook and canary windows by Fri.

[09:41] Anika B: I'll schedule the windows and reserve oncall.

[09:45] Emily C: I'll draft the compliance checklist.

[09:49] Raj P: will share cost spreadsheet.

[09:53] Priya K: Great — recap in the notes and I'll post to #prod-release. Meeting adjourned. Thanks everyone.

[10:00] -- End of transcript (some speaker labels may be approximated; minor transcription errors present)
